hints.content: We have to factor a $3$ out of the denominator in order to rewrite the expression as a geometric series.

We now have a geometric series with first term $a\text{ }=\text{ }1$ and common ratio $r\text{ }=\text{ }\displaystyle-\frac{1}{3}x^2$, with a constant multiplier of $\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}$ in front.

Therefore, the series is as follows.


$\displaystyle\frac{1}{3}\Big[1-\frac{1}{3}x^2+\frac{1}{9}x^4+\ldots +\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)^n x ^{2n}+\ldots \Big]$

$\displaystyle = \frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{9}x^2+\frac{1}{27}x^4+\ldots +\frac{1}{3}\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)^n  x  ^{2n}+\ldots $
